title: Skipping for Weight Loss: How Beginners Can Start
intro: Skipping is simple cardio you can do on your porch, in the corridor or in the living room in 10 minutes. No rope? No problem, just do ropeless skipping with the same hand movements.
muscles: Calves, thighs, glutes, shoulders and arms, with your core stabilising your body. It also trains your heart and coordination.
steps: Step on the middle of the rope; the handles should reach your armpits. No rope? Just swing your hands.
Keep your elbows close to your body and turn the rope with your wrists.
Jump low, 1-2 cm is enough, using the balls of your feet.
Land softly with your knees slightly bent.
Start with 30 seconds of jumping, 30 seconds of rest. Repeat 8-10 times.
mistakes: Jumping too high. This tires you out quickly and puts impact on your knees.
Turning the rope with your whole arm until your shoulders get tired fast.
Jumping on hard cement without shoes. Wear sports shoes and find a softer surface like an exercise mat.
easier: Do a step skip: alternate lifting your feet like a slow jog while swinging the rope. Or rest longer, for example 20 seconds of jumping, 40 seconds of rest.
harder: Increase to 45-60 seconds of jumping, 15-30 seconds of rest. Try alternating feet (jogging step) or add more sets.
dose: A total of 5-10 minutes of jumping (e.g. 10 sets x 30 seconds), 3 times a week with a rest day in between.
safety: Stop if you have shin, calf, knee or ankle pain that doesn't go away after rest. If you have joint problems or a higher body weight, start with the step skip or see a physio first.

faq.q: How many calories does 10 minutes of skipping burn?
faq.a: A rough estimate is 80-130 kcal, depending on your body weight and speed. That's about the same as half a plate of white rice, so combine it with controlled food portions.

faq.q: Can skipping slim down my tummy?
faq.a: No exercise removes fat from just one spot. Skipping helps burn energy, and when your eating and daily movement are under control, fat will come off from your whole body including your tummy, at your body's own pace.

faq.q: Do I have to wear shoes?
faq.a: Highly recommended. Sports shoes help absorb impact and protect your feet, especially on cement or tiled floors.
